skill.name: clinvar-database
skill.description: Query NCBI ClinVar for clinical variant interpretation, data access, bulk downloads, and VCF annotation workflows.
skill.summary: Use ClinVar data to search, interpret, download, and annotate human genetic variants.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: The skill is a legitimate ClinVar reference and workflow guide with no prompt injection or malicious intent found. Most static hits are documentation false positives, but FTP-based downloads and a curl-to-shell installer example create real transport and remote-code-execution risk for users who follow those examples.

remediation.issue: Remote installer is executed directly through sh -c.
remediation.suggestion: Replace the curl-to-shell installer with instructions to download over HTTPS when available, verify the script checksum or signature, inspect it, and then run it explicitly.

remediation.issue: Bulk download examples use FTP endpoints.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer HTTPS mirrors for NCBI downloads when supported, or document integrity checks such as checksums and release validation before processing data.

remediation.issue: Several examples encourage command-line processing of large external datasets.
remediation.suggestion: Add guidance to quote shell variables, validate downloaded filenames, and run examples in a controlled working directory.

Use pandas or command-line tools for rapid filtering and analysis.

content.value_statement: ClinVar data can be difficult to search, interpret, and integrate into genomic workflows. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code structured guidance for ClinVar queries, clinical significance review, bulk data access, and variant annotation.
actual_capabilities: Explains ClinVar search patterns for genes, conditions, variants, chromosomes, and clinical significance.
Guides use of NCBI E-utilities endpoints for search, summary, fetch, and related-record workflows.
Summarizes ClinVar clinical significance terms, review status levels, and conflict handling considerations.
Documents bulk ClinVar file formats, including XML, VCF, and tab-delimited releases.
Provides examples for annotating VCF files and filtering ClinVar datasets with common bioinformatics tools.
Highlights important limits such as VUS uncertainty, genome build alignment, rate limits, and incomplete VCF coverage.
limitations: It does not provide medical advice or replace review by a genetics professional.
It depends on public ClinVar data, which can contain outdated, conflicting, or incomplete submissions.
It does not automatically verify downloaded files or manage local database infrastructure.
Some examples rely on external tools and network access that must be configured by the user.

use_cases.title: Prioritize pathogenic variants in a gene
use_cases.description: Search ClinVar for variants in a target gene and filter by clinical significance and review status.

use_cases.title: Annotate sequencing results
use_cases.description: Use ClinVar VCF guidance to add clinical significance fields to a local variant call set.

use_cases.title: Build a reproducible ClinVar dataset
use_cases.description: Choose the right ClinVar release format and document versioned bulk download workflows.

prompt_templates.title: Search one gene
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the ClinVar skill to help me search for pathogenic variants in BRCA1. Include the query terms and explain the review status I should prioritize.

prompt_templates.title: Interpret one variant record
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the ClinVar skill to explain how I should evaluate a ClinVar record with uncertain significance and conflicting submitter interpretations.

prompt_templates.title: Plan VCF annotation
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the ClinVar skill to outline a safe workflow for annotating my GRCh38 VCF with ClinVar clinical significance and review status fields.

prompt_templates.title: Design a local ClinVar mirror
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the ClinVar skill to design a reproducible monthly ClinVar bulk download and parsing workflow. Include format choice, version tracking, validation, and update checks.

output_examples.output: The skill would suggest a ClinVar query for CFTR with pathogenic clinical significance and expert panel or practice guideline review status, then recommend checking accession details and evidence before clinical use.

output_examples.input: Annotate a tumor VCF with ClinVar.
output_examples.output: The skill would help match the genome build, select the ClinVar VCF file, add clinical significance fields, and warn that ClinVar interpretation may differ for somatic and germline contexts.

output_examples.input: Choose between XML and VCF downloads.
output_examples.output: The skill would recommend XML for full evidence and submission details, VCF for coordinate-based pipeline annotation, and tab-delimited files for quick summaries.

best_practices: Record the ClinVar release date, genome build, and access method for every analysis.
Prefer higher review status records and treat conflicting interpretations as requiring manual review.
Validate downloaded files and keep API requests within NCBI rate limits.
anti_patterns: Do not treat a VUS classification as evidence for clinical action.
Do not mix GRCh37 and GRCh38 coordinates in the same annotation workflow.
Do not run remote installer commands or FTP download scripts without verification.

faq.question: Can this skill diagnose a patient?
faq.answer: No. It supports data access and interpretation workflows, but clinical decisions require qualified genetics professionals.

faq.question: Which ClinVar format should I use?
faq.answer: Use XML for complete evidence, VCF for genomic coordinate annotation, and tab-delimited files for quick summaries.

faq.question: Does it support both GRCh37 and GRCh38?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance covers ClinVar files and considerations for both genome builds.

faq.question: Can it help with conflicting interpretations?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains how to compare review status, submitter evidence, dates, and expert panel records.

faq.question: Does it require an NCBI API key?
faq.answer: No for basic use. An API key can increase NCBI E-utilities rate limits when making automated requests.

faq.question: Is bulk download supported?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill documents ClinVar XML, VCF, and tab-delimited bulk download workflows and their tradeoffs.
